header.running_head: The Spending of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA)

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ (for Hijrah), Abu Bakr (RA) took along all the money he had, which amounted to five or six thousand Dirhams. My grandfather Abu Quhaafa (RA) who had lost his sight then came home. He said, 'By Allaah! I expect that together with alarming you by his leaving, Abu Bakr has also alarmed you with his money (by taking it all along with him).' I said, 'Not at all, dear grandfather. He has left plenty of money with us.' I then gathered some stones and placed them in the dish in which my father usually put his money. Thereafter, I covered it with a cloth and took his hand saying, 'Here, grandfather. Put your hand on this money.' He put his hand on it and (thinking that it was Dirhams) said, 'Then there is no problem. If he has left this money for you, he has done very well. There should be sufficient money here to see to your needs.' By Allaah! My father had not left a thing for us but all that I wished to do by this was to put the old man's heart at rest."[^1]
The narration has already passed in which it is stated that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) spent all of his four thousand Dirhams for the Tabook expedition.
The Spending of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA)
His Spending on the 'expedition of Difficulty' and the Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ About Him

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Khabbaab Sulami (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Khabbaab Sulami (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a sermon in which he encouraged the Sahabah (RA) to spend on the 'expedition of difficulty' (the expedition to Tabook). Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then said, "I shall provide a hundred camels together with their saddle blankets and saddles." Rasulullaah ﷺ then stepped down a step of the pulpit and again encouraged the Sahabah (RA). This time again Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) stood up and said, "I shall provide another hundred camels together with their saddle blankets and saddles." Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) says that he then saw Rasulullaah ﷺ shaking his hand as a person does when expressing wonder. A narrators by the name of Abdus Samad demonstrated this action by taking out his hand and shaking it. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "After this, Uthmaan need not carry out any other (optional) deed."[^2]

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ gave encouragement three times and that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) took it upon himself to provide three hundred camels together with their saddle blankets and saddles. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) says, "I was present there as Rasulullaah ﷺ stood on the pulpit saying, 'No sin can harm Uthmaan after this' or he said, 'No sin can harm Uthmaan after this day.'"[^3]
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.179). Ahmad and Tabraani have reported a similar narration but Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.59) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.5 Pg.4). Abu Nu'aym has also reported the narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.59).
